title: Episode 1 — What Is a Concussion?

sections.title: Hook
sections.onScreenText: What actually happens when you get a concussion?

voiceover.text: So… what actually happens to your brain when you get a concussion?
A concussion is a type of brain injury caused by a bump, blow, or jolt to the head—or even a hit to the body that makes the brain move rapidly inside the skull.
Even when there's no obvious damage on a scan, that sudden movement can temporarily disrupt how brain cells communicate and how the brain uses energy.
That can lead to symptoms like headache, dizziness, fatigue, brain fog, trouble concentrating, memory problems, or sensitivity to light and noise.
And here's something important: you do not have to lose consciousness to have a concussion. In fact, most people with concussions do not.
Symptoms can also show up right away—or develop hours or even days later. That's why it's important to pay attention to how you're feeling after an injury.
If you think you've had a concussion, stop the activity and get evaluated by a qualified professional.
A concussion is a brain injury. I'm your brain—let's learn together.

endCard.subtitle: Concussion & Brain Health
